A furlong is a unit of distance — a way of measuring how long a stretch of land or a path is.

One furlong equals one-eighth of a mile. If you imagine a mile cut into 8 equal pieces, each piece is one furlong. In more concrete terms:

  • 1 furlong = 220 yards
  • 1 furlong = 660 feet
  • 1 furlong ≈ 201 meters (roughly two football fields end to end)
  • 8 furlongs = 1 mile

So it sits between a meter and a mile on the scale of distances — not tiny, not enormous.

In everyday modern life, almost nobody uses furlongs. The word has survived almost entirely in one specific world: horse racing.

When a horse race is announced, its distance is described in furlongs and miles. You will hear things like:

  • "A race over 6 furlongs" (= ¾ of a mile, a short sprint)
  • "A race over 1 mile and 2 furlongs" (= 10 furlongs total)
  • "A race over 1 mile and 4 furlongs" (= 12 furlongs = 1.5 miles, a longer race)

Horse racing commentators, trainers, jockeys, and bettors all use this unit fluently. If you ever watch or follow horse racing — anywhere in the English-speaking world, including the UK, USA, Australia, or India — you will encounter furlongs constantly.

Outside horse racing, you might occasionally see the word used in farming or surveying contexts in older texts or in parts of the world where traditional measurements are still used, but this is rare today.
How to Think About It Instinctively

The best mental anchor: one furlong is roughly a two-minute walk. A fit person walks about 100 meters per minute, so 201 meters takes roughly two minutes at a relaxed pace.

For a horse, one furlong at a full gallop takes about 10–12 seconds.

Another anchor: think of a standard athletics running track. The straight portion on each side of an oval track is about 100 meters. One furlong is just about twice that straight — not far at all for a horse, but a meaningful sprint distance.
Using the Word in a Sentence

• "The horse won by a length in a race of seven furlongs."
  • "The two farms were separated by about three furlongs of open land."
  • "They were still furlongs away from the finish line when the leaders crossed it."

In that third example, "furlongs away" is used loosely to mean far behind — a figurative use that occasionally appears in writing.

To summarize cleanly: a furlong is a traditional unit of distance equal to one-eighth of a mile (about 201 meters). It belongs to the imperial system of measurement (the same system that uses miles, yards, and feet). Today, its practical use is almost entirely confined to horse racing, where it remains the standard way of describing race distances. If you understand that 8 furlongs = 1 mile, you can always work out any horse race distance instantly.
